newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
MAJOR IS OFF TO THE PALACE
There is increasing speculation that today PM John Major will name the election date for 1 May. Despite a huge deficit in the opinion polls Major is still confident that the Conservatives can win.
MARKETS BRACED FOR ELECTION DATE TEST

Many observers believed that the London market is relaxed about the prospect of a Labour victory in the General Election. The Footsie is likely to fall today because a number of companies are to go ex-dividend. A number of retailers will report results this week.
BLAIR PLANS TO RING-FENCE THE CO-OPS

The Labour Party is likely to endorse a bill being drafted by the United Kingdom Co-operatives Council which will protect Co-ops against hostile take-over bids. Andrew Regan of Lanica Trust is considering a hostile bid for Britain's two largest Co-ops.
PNG-related stock suffered badly on the Sydney Stock Exchange after reports of military action by the Papua New Guinea army against the country's Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan.
PACER STEPPING UP ITS HI-TECH PERFORMANCE

American technology firm Pacer Infotec appears to have rehabilitated itself after a dubious start on the Unlisted Securities Market. Profits were up to $1.48m for last year despite a probe into the acquisition of Infotec Development. House brokers Beeson Gregory expect profits to continue to rise and there is also speculation about a Nasdaq quote this year.

MAID TO MEASURE FOR PROFITS Despite fourth quarter losses in 1996 electronic information services provider MAID built up revenues and kept control of costs. It is likely to make considerable profits in the 1997 financial year.
